concept_mcqs.stem:
Your bank uses value dates. The EBS variant in SAP is currently set to post line items on the value date, not the statement date. You import the June 30 statement with this extract and try to auto-clear the bank clearing account:
```text
Statement date: 2026-06-30
Opening balance: 10,000.00
Lines:
  2026-06-28 POS Card Purchase           -150.00  (value date 2026-06-28)
  2026-06-30 Monthly Bank Fee             -25.00  (value date 2026-06-30)
  2026-06-30 Incoming Transfer           1,200.00 (value date 2026-07-01)
Closing balance: 11,025.00
```
GL 113100 Bank Clearing has an open incoming item of 1,200 posted on 2026-06-30 awaiting clearing. After EBS posting, which outcome occurs and why?
options: The 1,200 remains open because the EBS posts it on 2026-07-01, so it cannot clear the 2026-06-30 open item.
The 1,200 is posted as a new open item on 2026-06-30 but marked for future clearing automatically at rollover.
All three lines post on 2026-06-30 per statement date and fully clear the open item.
The 1,200 clears because the reference and amount match; value date does not affect clearing.
concept_mcqs.explanation: With posting on value date, the incoming transfer is posted on 2026-07-01. It cannot clear an open item from 2026-06-30 in the June period. The fee and POS post and clear within June; the 1,200 remains open until July or until you change posting logic.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: Tempting because matching by amount/reference is typical, but the posting date/period must allow clearing. C: Would be true if variant posted on statement date, but it is set to value date. D: SAP does not auto-flag future clearing rollover like this; clearing occurs when both sides exist in the same account/clearing transaction.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You posted an accrual via FAGL
a03/Accrual Engine at month-end with this header:
```text
Doc: 190000123
Posting date: 2026-06-30
Amount: 85,000 expense accrual (Dr Expense, Cr Accrued Liability)
Reversal date: 2026-07-10
```
The supplier invoice for 85,000 posts on 2026-07-02. What is the effect on July results until the reversal posts?
options: June becomes overstated because the system backdates the reversal to 2026-06-30.
July is overstated by 85,000 until 2026-07-10, then corrected by the accrual reversal.
No impact; SAP auto-adjusts the reversal date to 2026-07-01 when the invoice posts.
July is understated until 2026-07-10 because the liability reverses late.
concept_mcqs.explanation: The accrual remains on the books until the scheduled reversal on 2026-07-10. When the invoice posts on 2026-07-02, July temporarily has both the accrual and the invoice, overstating expense until the reversal entry on 07-10.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: SAP does not auto-shift reversal dates when related invoices post. C: Understatement would require an early reversal; here it's late. D: The reversal does not backdate to June.

concept_mcqs.stem:
At period-end you need to accrue unbilled services. Local VAT rules: input tax can only be claimed upon valid tax invoice. You have this invoice and an additional unbilled service:
```text
Posted AP invoice (has tax invoice):
  Base: 10,000 | VAT 18%: 1,800 | Total: 11,800
Unbilled service (no invoice yet):
  Estimated base: 5,000
```
How should you post the period-end accrual for the unbilled service?
options: Dr Expense 5,000; Cr Accrued Liability 5,000; reverse next period; book input VAT only when invoice arrives.
Dr GR/IR 5,000; Cr Accrued Liability 5,000 so VAT derives automatically.
Dr Expense 5,000; Dr Input VAT 900; Cr Accrued Liab 5,900; reverse next period.
Dr Suspense 5,000; Cr Accrued Liability 5,000; record VAT when accrual is cleared.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Without a tax invoice you generally cannot claim input VAT. Accrue the net expense only and reverse it next period. Recognize input VAT when the supplier tax invoice arrives.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: Tempting because it mirrors the invoiced case, but it violates the tax point rule. C: GR/IR is for goods receipts/invoice receipts matching, not generic service accruals. D: Using a suspense account does not address tax compliance; the correct issue is not posting VAT until invoiced.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Your month-end run left several internal orders with non-zero balances although all costs should be fully moved to final cost centers. The run log was:
```text
21:00 KO88 Settlement of internal orders (status: green)
22:00 KSU5 Assessment: Overhead from CC-OVH to receiver internal orders (status: green)
23:00 Checks: 6 orders show residual balances exactly equal to the assessed overhead
```
Which one action will clear the residuals without any reposting of primary costs?
options: Re-run assessment before settlement next month only; residuals will self-correct.
Re-open the period and run CO-FI reconciliation (RFUMSV00) first, then close again.
Run a distribution (KSV5) from final cost centers back to orders to net the balances, then settle again.
Re-run KO88 settlement after the KSU5 assessment so the assessed overhead on orders settles to the final receivers.
concept_mcqs.explanation: You assessed overhead to the orders after settling them, creating new order debits. Re-running settlement after assessment moves those secondary costs from the orders to their final receivers as per the settlement rules.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: Waiting does not fix the sequencing error. B: Reconciliation does not move costs between CO objects. D: Back-distributing from final receivers is the wrong direction and adds noise; simply settle the new debits.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Consider this master-data change mid-month:
```text
Cost center: CC100
Profit center assignment:
  2026-01-01 to 2026-06-14 -> PC-A
  From 2026-06-15          -> PC-B
Postings in June:
  2026-06-01 Primary expense 10,000 to CC100
  2026-06-20 Primary expense 5,000 to CC100
```
Assuming no profit center realignment or repostings are executed, how will June profit center P&L reflect these postings?
options: All 15,000 on PC-B because the latest assignment overrides within the month.
10,000 on PC-A and 5,000 on PC-B.
Split between PC-A and PC-B pro-rata by days in month.
All 15,000 on PC-A because the initial assignment dominates the month.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Profit center is derived at posting time. Historical line items retain their derived profit center. Without realignment/repostings, the 06-01 posting remains on PC-A and the 06-20 posting goes to PC-B.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Tempting if one believes master data is retroactive; it is not for existing line items. C: Also assumes retroactivity in the other direction. D: Day-weighting does not occur; derivation is per line item at its posting time.

concept_mcqs.stem:
During KO88 you get residual cost of 8,400 on order IO-7001. The allocation structure is defined as:
```text
Allocation structure AS01
  Assignments:
    Group CE_PRIM -> receiver CC (includes CE 600000-699999)
Settlement rule: 100% to CC200
Order actuals this period:
  620100: 12,000
  741500: 8,400
```
Why does 8,400 remain on the order?
options: 741500 is a secondary cost element; secondary costs never settle on expense orders.
Settlement profile lacks "Full settlement" and only settles to zero at year-end.
Receiver CC200 is locked; settlement skipped for that portion.
741500 is not covered by the allocation structure range; extend the assignment to include it.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Only 600000-699999 are assigned to settle. Cost element 741500 sits outside the assignment and is therefore not picked up by settlement. Extend the allocation structure to include it (or map to a different receiver).
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: Sounds plausible but depends on config; the real blocker shown is the missing mapping. C: Profile controls timing/requirements, not element selection here. D: A locked receiver would error out, not leave an unflagged residual matching an unmapped element.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You review a CO document created by assessment:
```text
CO Doc 500045
  Line 10: Sender CC-ADM, CE 930000 (Assessment)   +20,000
  Line 20: Receiver CC-OPS, CE 930000 (Assessment) -20,000
```
Which statement about its visibility in external financial statements is correct (classic ECC without Universal Journal)?
options: It appears in FI only at period close after CO-FI reconciliation.
It appears in FI as an expense in P&L because all CO postings update FI.
It does not appear in the FI trial balance because CE 930000 is a secondary cost element posted only in CO.
It updates FI balance sheet only, not P&L, because it is an internal reclassification.
concept_mcqs.explanation: In classic ECC, assessments post with secondary cost elements in CO and do not create FI postings. They affect CO reports but not the FI trial balance or P&L.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: True only in S/4 with Universal Journal where secondary cost elements are GL accounts. C: Assessments affect costs, not BS-only reclassifications. D: CO-FI reconciliation is a report/control, not a posting step that brings CO documents into FI.

concept_mcqs.stem: You run an assessment from CC-S (PC=PC1) to CC-R (PC=PC2) using secondary CE 930000. After the run, profit center reporting shows different PCs on sender and receiver. What shifts in reporting should you expect?
options: Costs move from PC1 to PC2 in CO profit center reports; external FI P&L totals remain unchanged.
External FI P&L moves from PC1 to PC2 because assessment reposts primary costs.
Costs stay on PC1 because assessment does not change profit center attribution.
Both CO and FI totals reduce because assessment eliminates internal costs.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Assessment reposts costs with secondary elements to the receivers. CO profit center actuals shift from PC1 to PC2. External FI P&L totals are unchanged because no new primary postings are created.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Assessment specifically moves attribution to receivers. C: It does not create/alter primary FI postings in classic ECC. D: Internal allocations do not eliminate costs; they reassign them within the entity.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Your EBS posting rules include these mappings:
```yaml
posting_rules:
  NCHK: bank_check
  FEE:  bank_charges
  POS:  card_sales
# No rule maintained for NTRF (incoming transfer)
```
The imported bank statement has a line with code NTRF and a customer reference. What is the likely system outcome for that line?
options: It is ignored during import; you must manually key the bank line before you can clear.
It is routed to the post-processing list as an exception; no clearing occurs until a rule is added or it is handled manually.
It posts as a memo item and auto-clears based on amount matching only.
It posts using the NCHK rule because both are incoming codes.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Without a mapping rule, SAP cannot determine postings for NTRF. The item goes to post-processing (FEBAN) for manual assignment, and no clearing happens automatically.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: SAP does not guess by similarity of codes. C: Memo items do not auto-clear based on amount without a rule. D: The line is imported but parked for manual action; it is not dropped.

concept_mcqs.stem: An internal order IO-9001 belongs to company code 100. Its settlement rule points 100% to cost center CC-200 in company code 200. Both company codes share controlling area CA01, but intercompany cost accounting is NOT configured. What happens when you run KO88?
options: The system posts within company code 100 only and ignores the receiver in 200.
The system settles statistical values only; the primary costs remain on the order.
The system errors and does not post; you must enable intercompany cost accounting and maintain intercompany clearing accounts to allow cross-company settlement.
The system posts intercompany FI documents automatically even without configuration because the controlling area is the same.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Cross-company settlement requires intercompany cost accounting settings and clearing accounts. Without them, settlement raises an error and does not post.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: SAP does not silently ignore an invalid receiver; it blocks posting. C: Intercompany postings are never automatic without configuration. D: There is no "statistical-only" fallback in KO88 for this case; it simply errors.

scenario_questions.scenario:
You are closing June. The bank statement shows end-of-month items that do not fully match the GL. Here are the artefacts:
```text
Bank statement (statement date 2026-06-30):
  06/28 POS Purchase                   -150.00 (value date 06/28)
  06/30 Monthly Bank Fee                -25.00 (value date 06/30)
  06/30 Incoming Customer Transfer    1,200.00 (value date 07/01)
GL 113100 Bank Clearing (as of 2026-06-30):
  Open item: +1,200.00 from customer payment (posted 06/30)
  No posting yet for bank fee
  POS Purchase of 150.00 posted 06/28, open for clearing
Bank main account 111000 shows 11,025.00 closing per statement.
EBS variant currently posts on value date.
```
Management wants June closed without misstating cash or AR. You can change June postings, but you cannot change the bank statement or reissue it.
scenario_questions.task: Decide the specific steps you will execute to reconcile and close June. Identify which items will auto-clear, which require manual postings or timing adjustments, the exact journal entries you will book (accounts and dates), and any configuration change (if any) you would propose for future months. Justify each decision against the artefacts and the restriction that EBS posts on value date.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
- Auto-clear POS 150.00 in June: EBS posts and clears the existing 150.00 open item in clearing account because both sides are in June.
- Post bank fee 25.00 as Dr Bank Charges (P&L) Cr Bank Main 111000 dated 2026-06-30 (if EBS did not create it automatically) or accept the EBS posting if configured. Evidence: fee has value date 06/30; it is a June cash movement.
- Do not attempt to clear the 1,200.00 in June because EBS posts it on 07/01 (value date) creating a July-side item. Leave the 06/30 +1,200 clearing open item uncleared at June close; AR is not misstated because the customer subledger is already cleared; cash is correctly not increased in June.
- Optional: temporarily park a June 30 bank-in-transit if policy requires zeroing clearing at month-end, with reversing entry on 07/01. Many organizations avoid this and accept the timing difference; provide policy rationale.
- For future months: recommend switching EBS to post on statement date if policy is to minimize timing differences, or keep value-date posting but update the close checklist to tolerate this reconciling item.
- Document reconciled bank balance: GL 111000 + uncleared 1,200.00 equals statement 11,025.00.

rubric.criterion: Correctly identifies which items clear in June vs remain open given value-date posting
Proposes correct journals (accounts, dates) for bank fee and any necessary in-transit policy entry (or argues no entry with sound rationale)
Explains impact on AR/cash and why leaving the 1,200 open does not misstate June
Future control/design recommendation on EBS posting date and/or checklist treatment, tied to the scenario

scenario_questions.scenario:
Your entity accrues month-end expenses for services received without invoices. VAT is 18% and can only be claimed on receipt of a valid invoice. Closing data:
```text
Item A: Consulting completed 06/29, PO exists, no invoice. Estimated 40,000.
Item B: Freight delivered 06/30, carrier invoice confirmed will be dated 07/05. Est. 12,000.
Item C: Software subscription July-Aug (prepaid), invoice dated 06/28 total 6,000 + VAT.
```
Finance wants to minimize July corrections and remain VAT-compliant.
scenario_questions.task: For A, B, and C, state the precise postings on 2026-06-30 and any reversals in July. Specify whether input VAT is posted on each and why. Include accounts, dates, and reversal dates. Briefly justify each choice.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
- Item A (unbilled consulting): 06/30 Dr Expense 40,000; Cr Accrued Liability 40,000. No input VAT because no tax invoice. Reverse 07/01.
- Item B (freight unbilled): 06/30 Dr Expense 12,000; Cr Accrued Liability 12,000. No input VAT. Reverse 07/01. When invoice dated 07/05 arrives, post 12,000 + 2,160 VAT and clear the reversal/expense accordingly.
- Item C (prepaid for July-Aug with invoice 06/28): On 06/28 initial AP posting Dr Prepaid (BS) 6,000; Dr Input VAT 1,080; Cr Vendor 7,080. On 06/30, defer nothing further (already prepaid). On 07/01 start monthly release: Dr Expense 3,000; Cr Prepaid 3,000 (repeat 08/01 for balance). VAT stays recognized in June based on the tax invoice date; no VAT reversals. Rationale: VAT only on valid invoice; accruals for unbilled exclude input tax; prepayments recognize VAT when invoiced and amortize the net over service period.

rubric.criterion: Correct accrual/deferral postings per item with appropriate accounts and dates
Correct VAT treatment and justification per local rule for each item
Correct reversal/release timing (07/01 for accruals; monthly deferral for prepaid)
Clarity connecting postings to compliance and minimization of July corrections

scenario_questions.scenario:
Marketing runs an internal order IO-MKTG to collect campaign costs, then settle to CC-SALES monthly. Data:
```text
Order type: ZEXP (expense), Settlement profile allows periodic full settlement
Allocation structure AS01 maps 600000-699999 to receiver CC
Actuals on IO-MKTG (June):
  610100 Media spend           90,000
  741200 Internal services     15,000
  650500 Agency fees           30,000
Settlement rule: 100% to CC-SALES (receiver OK)
KO88 run shows: Settled 120,000; Residual 15,000
```
Controller asks why a residual remains and how to fix it before close.
scenario_questions.task: Diagnose the root cause from the artefact and propose concrete corrective steps to achieve zero balance on IO-MKTG for June, without changing the business intent. Include any config/data changes and the sequence of reruns required.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
Root cause: Cost element 741200 (internal services) is outside the allocation structure mapping (600000-699999). Those secondary/other cost elements are not assigned for settlement, so they remain as residuals.
Fix: Extend AS01 to include 741200 (either by widening the range or adding a group) and assign it to receiver CC-SALES. If 741200 is a secondary CE and policy is not to settle secondary costs, repost it first to a mapped primary CE on the order using reposting (KB11N) or assess from the cost center rather than book to the order. Then re-run KO88 for June. Verify IO actual balance = 0 and receiver CC reflects the full 135,000 if policy allows settling that element, or 120,000 with the 15,000 handled via CO allocation if not.

rubric.criterion: Identifies unmapped cost element 741200 as the driver of the residual
Proposes a correct configuration/data remedy (extend allocation structure and/or repost/assess)
Specifies an execution sequence (adjust mapping/repost, then re-run KO88)
States the expected zero-balance outcome on the order and impact on receiver

scenario_questions.scenario:
In June, CC100 was reassigned from PC-A to PC-B on 06/15. Actuals:
```text
06/01 640100 Utilities   10,000  (posted to CC100 -> PC-A)
06/20 640100 Utilities    5,000  (posted to CC100 -> PC-B)
Assessment KSU5 (CE 930000) from CC-ADM (PC-A) to CC100 ran on 06/30 for 8,000.
Profit center P&L shows 18,000 on PC-A and 5,000 on PC-B, which management disputes.
```
They want all June utilities for CC100 on PC-B for reporting, with a clean audit trail.
scenario_questions.task: Recommend and justify a correction approach to achieve management’s reporting aim without violating accounting principles. Choose between profit center realignment, repostings, or leaving as-is with explanatory schedules. Detail the steps, impacts on FI vs CO, and controls you would apply.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
Two compliant approaches:
1) Profit center realignment (PCA/realignment tool) for FI primary postings dated 06/01 on CC100 from PC-A to PC-B. This preserves original documents and creates realignment records moving profit center attribution without changing amounts, supporting reporting on PC-B. Assessments (secondary costs) should also be realigned to PC-B for CC100 to keep CO/FI views consistent if tooling supports it.
2) Manual FI reposting (FB50/FB01 with document splitting/profit center in line items) to move the 10,000 from PC-A to PC-B with clear reference to the original document; then reverse the assessment or re-assess so secondary costs align with the new PC. This changes FI balances and requires strict documentation and approvals.
Justification: Master data is not retroactive; adjustments must be explicit. Controls: approval workflow, cross-check CO/FI tie-out post-adjustment, lock further postings, and maintain an audit trail mapping original doc numbers to adjustments. If policy forbids moving posted profit center on primary costs, leave as-is but add a management reporting adjustment schedule; document the variance and root cause.

rubric.criterion: Selects a valid method (realignment or reposting) and rejects retroactive master-data-only fixes
Describes concrete steps and how they impact FI vs CO (primary vs secondary costs)
Addresses controls/audit trail to keep the adjustment compliant and traceable

practical_tasks.title: Author a production-grade month-end Close Checklist (Bank, Tax, Accruals, Closing Tasks)
practical_tasks.brief: Design the actionable checklist your team will use to close a period covering bank reconciliation/EBS, tax awareness steps, accruals, and closing tasks. It must be execution-ready (owners, T-codes/reports, inputs/outputs, dependencies, evidence required) and sequenced to avoid rework.
acceptance_criteria: Submitted as a single file (CSV/XLSX/PDF) with at least these columns: ID, Task name, Module (Bank/Tax/Accrual/Close), SAP T-code/Report, Prerequisites, Inputs, Steps, Outputs, Owner/Role, Due day (relative to WD), Frequency, Controls, Evidence artifact filename, Completion check.

Includes concrete SAP artefacts for each task (e.g., FEBAN for EBS exceptions, FBL3N/BSI for GL, FAGL_FCV or valuation steps if used, FAGL
a03/Accrual Engine or FB50 accrual JV, KSU5/KSII/KO88 for CO period end checks).

Sequenced dependencies are explicit (e.g., run EBS import before GL reconciliation; run assessments before settlement where receivers are orders; run reconciliations after allocations and settlements).
Bank section covers: EBS import, unmatched items handling, bank fee posting, value-date policy, bank-to-GL reconciliation with tie-out math.
Tax section covers: rule on input VAT for unbilled, tax code review for period, tax report extraction (e.g., RFUMSV00) and review timing.
Accruals section covers: criteria for accrual vs deferral, reversal dates, sample entries, and sign-off.

Closing tasks section covers: CO allocations/settlements, CO-FI reconciliation review, open-item reviews (GR/IR, bank clearing), error handling, and period close steps (OB52/period variant referencing without config screenshots).
Each task row lists a concrete evidence artifact (report export/screenshot name) that an assessor can open to verify completion.
Checklist includes at least 20 tasks spanning all four areas and clearly marks the critical path.

rubric.criterion: Coverage and correctness across Bank, Tax, Accruals, and Closing Tasks (minimum 20 tasks)
Accurate sequencing and dependencies that prevent rework or residuals
Clarity and actionability (owners, T-codes/reports, inputs/outputs)
Evidence-driven controls (named artifacts per task; tie-out math where applicable)
Professional presentation and completeness (one coherent document)

practical_tasks.title: Build an end-to-end FI–CO integration case with cost centers, profit centers, and an internal order
practical_tasks.brief: In a sandbox or as a documented dry-run, execute an end-to-end flow showing how costs move from vendor invoice to internal order, get allocated/settled to a final cost center, and appear in profit center reporting. Include a period-end accrual and show that tax handling and FI–CO views reconcile.
acceptance_criteria: Submit a single zipped folder or PDF containing: (1) scenario narrative with org data, (2) master data sheet (CC, PC, IO with assignments and dates), (3) posting log with document numbers/dates/amounts, (4) period-end run log (allocations/settlements), (5) report exports.

Transactions included: one AP vendor invoice with tax posted to IO (primary CE), one manual month-end accrual reversed next month, one CO allocation (assessment or reposting) that touches the IO or the sending CC, and KO88 settlement of the IO to a final CC.

Provide four exhibits that tie numerically: (A) FI document for vendor invoice showing base and tax, (B) IO actuals report before and after settlement with zero residual, (C) receiver cost center actuals reflecting the settled amount, (D) profit center P&L showing where the cost ultimately resides.
Demonstrate VAT handling: show that input VAT from the invoice does not flow into CO cost totals and that the unbilled accrual (if any) excludes VAT and reverses on day 1 of the next period.

Include a reconciliation table that proves: Invoice base amount = IO actuals pre-settlement = Amount settled to CC = Profit center final cost (within rounding). Residual on IO at period-end must be 0.00.
All artefacts are legible exports or screenshots with dates; calculations are reproducible by an assessor using only the submission.

rubric.criterion: Completeness of the end-to-end flow (AP with tax, accrual with reversal, CO allocation/settlement)
Numerical tie-out across FI and CO with zero residual on the order and consistent PC reporting
Correct handling and documentation of VAT and its exclusion from CO cost flow
Quality and clarity of artefacts (master data, logs, reports) enabling independent verification
Cohesive narrative linking steps, controls, and outcomes
